summary.name: International Typographic Style (Swiss Style). The source lists it as a supplemental design reference under Graphic Design and Design Movements, not as a directly named style in its collection.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit cues: column grid, baseline alignment, repeated spacing, asymmetric composition, and generous negative space. Left-aligned sans-serif type with clear size hierarchy, black and white with restrained accents, and grid-aligned photography.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly suited to UI and product storytelling, editorial and minimalist layouts, and motion posters with staged geometric compositions. Inferred: posters, identity pieces, and typographic statements where grid and type carry the message. Data explainers need a supporting style.
summary.limitations: Adapt or omit when recomposition changes hierarchy without explaining the subject, when cropping hides key details, or when pinning disrupts layout. Two-color contrast checks do not guarantee readability over images, textures, video, or animated lighting. Unspecified: maximum duration, aspect ratios, and audience.
summary.palette: Suggested direction is black and white with one restrained red accent. Tokens: background #FFFFFF, foreground #000000, accent_1 #D32F2F, three discrete colors with gradients disabled. Foreground on background is 21:1 and background on accent_1 is 4.979:1. These are authored suggestions; task-supplied or approved palettes override them. Verify pairs on composited frames.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit guidance: animate along layout axes and settle elements on shared alignment points without disrupting reading order. Preserve deliberate sharp cuts and reading holds; easing is not required everywhere, and springs or overshoot are not inherent to this style. Optional pattern references (pinned hero, chaptered transition, swipe carousel, scroll storytelling) apply only when their scene supports them. Interactive variants need keyboard and reduced-motion behavior; video must not depend on live input.
summary.audio: Unspecified by the source for this style; no audio layer is assigned. Options offered as task-specific suggestions include background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence, chosen per topic and narrative. Speech must remain intelligible, with balanced levels, no clipping, and synchronized picture. No authorized audio assets are supplied.
summary.assetRequirements: Unspecified: no fonts, photography, or artwork are supplied. Sans-serif fonts must be loaded locally before rendering. Grid-aligned photography is required only if the chosen design uses it. Artwork can be authored in HTML, CSS, or SVG; tldraw exports are flattened unless layers are split deliberately.
summary.combinations: Suggested hybrids are style-097 for diagram and chart layers inside the column grid, with charts limited to black, white, and the red accent, and style-093 for kinetic headline statements using one sans-serif family with no springs. Avoid multi-hue categorical palettes, centered or rotated labels, and script or display faces. Use Swiss alone unless data or headlines must carry the piece.
summary.productionApproach: Style renderer: HTML/CSS with CSS Grid and loaded fonts, plus SVG aligned to the baseline grid. Motion engine: GSAP or Motion, with one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the default pipeline for assembly, timing, audio sync, validation, and export; Remotion is a conditional fallback only, with a recorded reason. chroma.js is optional for color checks. Verify seeks, key frames, decoded video, and audio. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production.
